items.stem: A linear system is unstable if any pole of its transfer function lies:

options.text: In the right half of the complex plane
options.rationale: Correct: a right-half-plane pole produces an unbounded response.

options.text: Exactly at the origin for a first-order system
options.rationale: Origin poles are marginal, handled case by case, not automatically unstable.

items.explanation: Correct: a right-half-plane pole produces an unbounded response.

items.stem: Which TWO describe the effect of PID terms? (Select TWO.)

options.rationale: Correct: the integral term drives steady-state error to zero.

options.text: Derivative action can reduce overshoot by anticipating change
options.rationale: Correct: derivative adds damping based on the rate of change.

options.text: Proportional action alone always removes steady-state error
options.rationale: Proportional-only control usually leaves a steady-state offset.

options.text: Integral action speeds up the system with no downside
options.rationale: Too much integral action increases overshoot and can destabilise.

items.explanation: Correct: the integral term drives steady-state error to zero.

items.stem: The key difference between closed-loop and open-loop control is that closed-loop:

options.text: Uses measured output as feedback to correct the input
options.rationale: Correct: feedback lets the controller respond to the actual output.
Closed-loop control relies on sensing the output.
Feedback often adds cost, not removes it.
Feedback can introduce instability if poorly designed.

items.explanation: Correct: feedback lets the controller respond to the actual output.
